title: acre formats a file, and the editor colors the v3 syntax
body:
`acre-gui` edits source in an egui `TextEdit` with colors from `lang::highlight`. Nothing reformats a file, and `highlight` predates v1 to v3 of the language: it colors a string as one run, with no markup inside it, and it treats `let` names as plain words.

## Proposal

- `lang::format` rewrites source into one layout: four-space indent per brace, single spaces between values, no space inside `( )`, at most one blank line in a row. It keeps comments and the line breaks the author chose between items, so a node written on one line stays on one line. It refuses a file that does not parse.
- `acre fmt FILE` formats in place, and `--check` reports whether a file would change. The GUI formats on a menu item and a shortcut.
- `highlight` marks the markup inside strings (`` ` ``, `**`, `{name`, `}`) and the words a `let` defines. The GUI paints each `#rrggbb` and each color `let` name on its own color.

The formatter works on the token stream, which already keeps every byte through the spans between tokens. It needs no new syntax tree.
